name: Jashobeam
title: David's Chief Warrior
summary: Jashobeam, also known as Joseb-Bassebet, was the leader of David's three mightiest warriors. He was a Hakmonite who, according to 2 Samuel 23, killed 800 men in one battle with his spear. He is regarded as the foremost among David's heroes and one of the most feared warriors in the United Kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as leader of David's three heroes
keyEvents.description: Jashobeam was recognized as the foremost of David's three mightiest warriors, a position of great honor and trust in David's kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Killed 800 men in one battle
keyEvents.description: In a single heroic feat, Jashobeam swung his spear against 800 enemies and killed them all in one fight, demonstrating his extraordinary combat skills.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In 1 Chronicles 11, he is mentioned by the name Jashobeam, son of Hakmoni, and it is told that he killed 300 men in one battle with his spear.

keyEvents.title: Part of David's inner circle of heroes
keyEvents.description: Josheb-Basshebeth belonged to the innermost circle of David's elite warriors, who played a crucial role in establishing and defending David's kingdom.

keyEvents.title: David's list of heroes
keyEvents.description: Josheb-Basshebeth is mentioned first in the famous list of David's heroes, a catalog of the bravest and most loyal warriors who served King David throughout his reign.
